2026-07-05-v1.92-closure.title: Resume TOFU fingerprint gate is in-band over the same (MITM-able) TLS fetch session — not transport-bound; buildClient() does not pass pinnedFingerprint to the HTTP transport
2026-07-05-v1.92-closure.scope: apps/web/src/lib/nexus/use-resume-fingerprint-gate.ts (in-band /cert-fingerprint fetch + compare); apps/web/src/lib/client-context.tsx buildClient() (no pinnedFingerprint → transport); apps/desktop/src-tauri/ (no reqwest/rustls cert-pin for remote daemon)
2026-07-05-v1.92-closure.note: Attack path: an active MITM that terminates TLS on the trusted LAN can serve the stored fingerprint string via the unauthenticated /cert-fingerprint endpoint (the comparison happens over the same compromised fetch session), pass the FingerprintGate, then capture X-API-Key on subsequent authenticated calls. Browser fetch cannot expose the server cert for pinning (JS limitation) — the browser/web-app surface TOFU is inherently weaker and is a documented V1.92 trade-off (raw-browser remote = non-goal). The REAL resolution is desktop (Tauri) transport-layer cert pinning: route remote-daemon HTTP through a Rust reqwest+rustls client with a custom certificate verifier that checks the served cert's SHA-256 against pinnedFingerprint. Originally target V1.94; re-queued to V1.95 because V1.94 scoped to desktop-onboarding UX work with no security-surface overlap. Medium severity bounded by the trusted-LAN threat model (V1.92 assumes trusted LAN; exploit requires active MITM on that LAN).
